title: The battleship that was not finished

facts.text: Jean Bart was the second battleship of France's Richelieu class, designed to carry eight 380 mm (15 inch) guns in two four gun turrets and to make 32 knots.
In June 1940, with German troops closing in, she was still unfinished in the shipyard at Saint-Nazaire.
Workers rushed boilers and turbines aboard, and on 19 June 1940 she slipped out of the estuary to escape capture, grounding briefly in the dark on the way.
She reached Casablanca on 22 June 1940 with only her forward turret armed. The second turret had no guns at all.
On 8 November 1942, when the Americans landed in Morocco, she opened fire on the U.S. fleet from her berth in Casablanca harbor.
Shells from the battleship USS Massachusetts hit her that morning and jammed her one working turret.
On 10 November, dive bombers from the carrier USS Ranger hit her with two 1,000 pound bombs, starting fires and flooding that left her settled by the stern.
U.S. Navy photos taken on 16 November 1942 show the damage from 16 inch shells and 1,000 pound bombs.
France finished her after the war. She was declared complete in 1955, went into reserve in 1957, and was struck from the navy list in 1970.

declassified.fact: The turret that Massachusetts jammed on the morning of 8 November was not out for long. Workers cut away the bent steel and had it firing again by that evening, which is why the Navy had to come back for her with dive bombers two days later.
